capabilities: Create exercise projects via a five-step workflow that generates a .exercise.yml manifest and inserts a viewer block
Render read-only viewers with a file tree, syntax highlighting, line annotations, media previews, and expected-output comparison
Copy exercises to a local destination outside the vault with injected comments and optional IDE launch
Insert viewers for existing exercises and manage copy-destination ignore rules
Configure preview size limits and Quartz exclusion patterns
extras: Desktop-only: it writes outside the vault only after a copy destination is chosen and makes no network requests. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Obsidian has no way to author, render, and hand off self-contained programming exercises with per-file notes, expected outputs, and a path into a local coding environment.

relations.evidence: The companion Quartz plugin reads the generated contract.
offer VS Code for Python-only projects or IntelliJ IDEA for Java-only projects
offer VS Code for Python-only projects or IntelliJ IDEA for Java-only projects

requires.name: VS Code or IntelliJ IDEA (optional launcher on PATH)
Quartz site (optional for root index panels)

summary: Desktop-only plugin for creating, previewing, and copying read-only programming exercise projects with annotated files and generated YAML manifests.
